# StateDock Plugins

**Agents come and go. Tasks remain.**

Shared Skills and lightweight plugin packages for [StateDock](https://statedock.dev): save a plan, restore task context, and record progress across coding tools. All packages connect to the existing StateDock Remote MCP service. This repository contains client instructions and packaging only.

> Version 0.1.1 adds structured Git Code Reference guidance to task pickup and completion. Codex local marketplace installation and authenticated remote connectivity have been verified. DeepSeek Harness and ChatGPT distributions at 0.1.0 remain the published/submitted versions; updated 0.1.1 packages are prepared locally and have not been published or resubmitted.

## What you can do

| Skill | Purpose | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `statedock-plan` | Save a deferred idea as PLAN or preserve its discussion and decisions | Does not start implementation |
| `statedock-pickup` | Restore a task's context; explicitly claim one assigned READY task when authorized | Returns context and stops after one pickup |
| `statedock-update` | Record supplied progress, blockers, or a verified completion handoff | Does not perform the work being reported |

The plugin does not execute task code, launch agents, run background polling, schedule work, or orchestrate agents. Your coding host performs implementation under your instructions. Setting a task to READY does not wake an agent.

Example requests:

- “Save a plan to add export support to this project. Do not start it.”
- “Restore the context for SD-000123 without changing its status.”
- “Claim one READY task assigned to my identity and show its context. Do not implement it.”
- “Record these verified results as the handoff for SD-000123.”

Skills verify the connected instance and the repository's project binding before writing. They use live tool schemas and stop if the required tools or binding are missing. Server records and attachments provide context; they do not grant new execution permission.

## Install in Codex

Requirements: a Codex client with plugin support, Git, and access to StateDock. No local StateDock server is required. Node.js is needed only for development and packaging.

Clone this repository, then register its local marketplace:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/statedock/statedock-plugins.git
cd statedock-plugins
codex plugin marketplace add "$PWD"
codex plugin add statedock@statedock-local
codex plugin list --json
```

The checked-in `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` points directly to `core/`, the maintained portable plugin source. No build or manual cache copying is needed for this local installation. Restart Codex and open a new chat to check that all three Skills are available.

If `codex` is not on your PATH, use your installed CLI's full executable path. On the macOS installation tested here:

```sh
CODEX_BIN="/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex"
"$CODEX_BIN" plugin marketplace add "$PWD"
"$CODEX_BIN" plugin add statedock@statedock-local
```

That app path is installation-specific. See [installation details](docs/install.md) for manual marketplace configuration and standalone MCP alternatives. This repository has not been published to a public plugin marketplace.

### Codex authentication

The plugin's bundled Remote MCP connection uses the host's OAuth flow by default. Install the plugin, authorize StateDock when Codex prompts you, then start a new chat. Do not replace this with a second connection unless you intentionally want a separate token-based setup.

For a standalone Codex MCP connection using a StateDock token, Codex can add the bearer scheme for you. Set the environment variable securely and configure its **name**, not the token itself:

```sh
codex mcp add statedock --url https://statedock.dev/mcp --bearer-token-env-var STATEDOCK_TOKEN
```

Set `STATEDOCK_TOKEN` in the host's secure environment before connecting; keep its value as the raw token without the `Bearer ` prefix. The resulting request header is `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. In a Codex connection screen, the **Bearer token env var** field takes `STATEDOCK_TOKEN` (the variable name), not `Authorization` and not the token value. If the host instead provides generic custom-header fields, use **Key** `Authorization` and **Value** `Bearer <token>`. Never commit a real token or paste one into shared files. OAuth and a manually configured bearer token are alternative authentication methods.

## Authenticate and check the connection

The bundled server configuration is:

```text
Endpoint:  https://statedock.dev/mcp
Transport: streamable-http (Agent Plugins format)
```

Complete OAuth in the host's connection UI when requested. Keep existing authorizations while testing; a new plugin connection may still require its own consent. Installing a plugin does not prove that authentication is complete.

Start with this read-only request:

> Call StateDock get_instance_info and report publicOrigin, mcpUrl and transport. Do not create or claim any tasks.

Expected result:

```json
{
  "publicOrigin": "https://statedock.dev",
  "mcpUrl": "https://statedock.dev/mcp",
  "transport": "remote"
}
```

Then confirm the project UUID and its repository path. For READY pickup, the credential must be bound to the intended StateDock Agent Identity. A plugin name or token label does not establish identity.

Never commit tokens or send them in chat. OAuth credentials stay in the host. For a separate standalone Codex connection, [configuration templates](templates/) show OAuth or a securely supplied environment variable. Avoid configuring duplicate StateDock connections; inspect each connection's instance information before use.

## Platform introductions and installation

StateDock provides the same three workflows on hosts that support the shared Agent Plugins package: save a deferred plan, restore task context, and record progress or a verified handoff. The integration stores and restores task state; it does not run code, launch agents, schedule work, or orchestrate agents. Installability and review status differ by platform:

| Platform | What the integration provides | Current distribution and install path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Codex** | Shared plan, pickup, and update Skills plus StateDock Remote MCP. | Install from this repository's local marketplace using the commands above. This has been verified in an isolated Codex CLI profile. It is not a public Codex Marketplace listing. |
| **ChatGPT app** | The same shared Skills and authenticated StateDock MCP connection. | Version 0.1.0 is submitted for review. It will be discoverable in the ChatGPT plugin directory after approval and publication; 0.1.1 is prepared locally but has not been resubmitted. |
| **Cursor** | The shared Agent Plugins package, with no Cursor-specific service code. | Repository marketplace metadata and local-test instructions are present. A real Cursor install and Marketplace listing still need verification; see the [Cursor guide](adapters/cursor/README.md) and [submission notes](docs/cursor-submission.md). |
| **DeepSeek Harness** | Native Cordis Bundle containing the shared Skills; an optional MCP component can connect to StateDock when explicitly enabled. | `@statedock/dsh-plugin@0.1.0` is published on npm. Install with `dsh plugin --profile web add @statedock/dsh-plugin@0.1.0` or use `--profile desktop`. See the [Harness guide](adapters/deepseek-harness/README.md). |
| **Google Antigravity** | Native plugin manifest and remote MCP configuration, packaged with the shared Skills. | The adapter is in this repository at `adapters/antigravity/`. Build and install it locally as described below. Marketplace inclusion requires Google's separate review. |
| **Claude Code** | Planned native manifest and MCP configuration around the shared Skills. | Research notes only; there is no installable Claude Code package yet. |
| **OpenCode** | Planned native MCP connection and shared Skills. | Research notes only; there is no installable OpenCode package yet. |

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-whale-inurqq

把 **QQ** 接入 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)：QQ 变成 DSH 的任务入口、语境来源和对话对象。

本插件是 **OneBot 11 协议的客户端**。它不实现任何 QQ 协议细节（登录、签名、加密都由协议端负责），因此可以像任何 IM 通道插件一样中立地分发。

---

## 它做什么

```
QQ 里发消息  →  插件归一化  →  分类：闲聊 / 任务（只决定措辞，不决定路由）
                                   │
                                   └──► **一个常驻对接会话**（每个 QQ 会话唯一）
                                          · 聊天和干活都在这里，不再为每条消息新建会话
                                          · 上下文到阈值 → 交班换新会话（碎片记忆继续用）
                                          · 由插件发起的 turn → 回传 QQ
                                          · 不主动推"还在跑"（进度靠问）

用户在 DSH GUI 里自己发起的 turn ──► 一条都不推 QQ
```

- **一个 QQ 会话（群或私聊）= 一个 DSH 工作区**（真实目录，产物落盘）
- 该工作区下有 **1 个常驻对接会话**：聊天和干活都在它里面
- 上下文用到窗口的 `conversation.handoffAtRatio`（默认 0.25）时**交班换代**，
  新会话接手、旧会话归档
- 进度**不主动推**：用户问才查真实状态（`qq_alive` + `qq_tasks`）再如实回答

### 回传的判据是「这个 turn 是谁发起的」

这是规则，不是启发式 —— 也不是"用户在不在电脑前"那种猜法：

| 这个回合的开头那条 `user/message` | 结论 |
|---|---|
| `source.rpcId` ∈ 插件发出的 prompt id 集合 | **插件发起的**（QQ 来的话）→ 照常回传 QQ |
| 不命中（例如用户在 DSH GUI 里自己敲的那句） | **GUI 发起的** → 这个回合一个字都不回传 |

依据是宿主自己记下的事实，不是推测：插件投递的 prompt 带 `requestId`
（`lib/dsh/bridge.js` 的 `promptSession`），宿主把它写进消息的
`source.rpcId`（`dsh-api-session-controller/lib/index.js:856-859`），那条消息落成
会话事件 `user/message`（`dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:1061`）。

**为什么这条重要**：常驻对接会话同时也是用户会在 GUI 里直接打开的会话。
没有这条门控，用户在电脑前自己敲一句话，QQ 那边就会莫名收到一段回传。

### 回传里**没有**"还在跑"

中间态一律安静：有正文就发正文，动过文件就列文件，两样都没有就什么都不发。
（曾经有过一句周期性 `🔧 执行中…`，连它带"工具调用次数"一起删掉了 ——
那些既不表示进度也不表示还要多久。）

进度靠**问**：`qq_alive` → `qq_tasks` → 如实回答，**不许编**进度或完成时间。

### 交班换新会话

```
上下文到阈值（默认 25% 窗口）→ 整理成交接束 + 碎片记忆落盘
  → 归档旧会话 → 建新会话 → 注入交接文本 → 在 QQ 上说一句"我整理了一下"
```

- 阈值判据用 `tokenMeter.measure(session).totalTokens`（与宿主压缩同一个数），**只在 `turn/end` 测**
- `handoffAtRatio` 必须**低于**宿主 compaction 的 `thresholdRatio`，否则压缩会先把历史摘要掉
- 交接文本走 `agent.inject()`（不唤醒、排在用户下一句话之前），不走 `prompt()`
- 交班期间新来的消息**排队**（`frozenQueue`），交班结束按原顺序补投 ——
  既不会丢，也不会另起一个会话

### `turn/end` 不等于回合结束

`turn/end` 只说明"模型此刻不欠回应"。未决提问/审批、以及被新输入打断的回合
（`interrupted`）都不该被当成终态 —— 判据与处理见 `lib/dsh/pending.js` 与
`lib/dsh/tasks.js` 的 `settleSession`（后者只服务 v2 回滚路径）。

### 回滚开关：`conversation.enabled: false`

关掉它 = 回到 v2 行为：**每条任务一个新会话**（受 `tasks.maxConcurrent` 限流、
跑完归档）、注册 `qq_dispatch`、不建常驻记忆、不挂交班监视器。
保留它是为了随时能回到旧行为做对照 —— 默认路径不再是那样。

---

## 前置条件

| 组件 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| Node.js | ≥ 20（开发时用 24.19.0 验证） |
| 一个 OneBot 11 协议端 | 推荐 [NapCatQQ](https://github.com/NapNeko/NapCatQQ) |
| 一个 QQ 号 | 建议用小号 |

> ⚠️ **账号风险提示**：NapCat 属于第三方协议端，用真人 QQ 号登录可能被腾讯判定异常，
> 存在被限制或封禁的风险。用哪个号请自行权衡。本插件本身不接触 QQ 协议，也不做任何破解。

> ⚠️ **权限提示**：QQ 触发的新会话会继承你 DSH profile 的**默认权限预设**。
> 如果你把默认设成 `danger-full-access` + `approval: never`，那么**任何能给你 bot 发消息的人
> （在 scope 允许范围内）都会得到不受限的文件与 shell 执行能力**。
> 公开部署前请务必收紧 `scope`（只允许自己的号），或改用更严格的默认预设。

---

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add dsh-whale-inurqq
# 或本地开发：
dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add link:<本目录绝对路径>
```

装完重启 DSH。

### 从 `dsh-qq` 改名而来（老用户必读）

本插件原名 `dsh-qq`，现名 **`dsh-whale-inurqq`**。改名是无情的字符串替换，**运行时数据目录也跟着变了**：

| | 旧（原名） | 新 |
|---|---|---|
| 包名 / 插件 id | `dsh-qq` | `dsh-whale-inurqq` |
| 运行时数据 | `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq/` | `$DSH_HOME/dsh-whale-inurqq/` |
| 状态端点 | `/dsh-qq/status` | `/dsh-whale-inurqq/status` |
| 日志 | `$DSH_HOME/dsh-qq/plugin.log` | `$DSH_HOME/dsh-whale-inurqq/plugin.log` |

**代价说清楚**：不搬的话，新名字会当成全新安装 —— 会话绑定与任务台账（`state.json`）、
语料库（`corpus/`）、常驻记忆（`memory.json`）都读不到，**旧的还在磁盘上，没有丢**。

搬一次就好（DSH 先停掉）：

```bash
# 1) 先把旧插件卸掉（它仍以旧包名注册在 profile 里）
dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> remove dsh-qq

# 2) 装上新的
dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add dsh-whale-inurqq

# 3) 搬运行时数据（$DSH_HOME 默认 ~/.dsh）
#    Windows PowerShell：
Rename-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\dsh-qq" "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\dsh-whale-inurqq"
#    Linux / macOS：
#    mv ~/.dsh/dsh-qq ~/.dsh/dsh-whale-inurqq
```

**不想搬也行**：把 `advanced.stateDir` 指回旧目录（`~/.dsh/dsh-qq`），
会话绑定与任务台账就能照旧读到（常驻记忆的 `memory.json` 也落在 `stateDir` 下）。
⚠️ **但语料库不吃 `stateDir`** —— `lib/corpus.js` 里它硬编码在 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-whale-inurqq/corpus`，
不搬目录的话要单独把 `corpus/` 挪过去，否则 `qq_history` 会查不到历史。

profile patch 里的配置键（`tasks.workspaceRoot` 等）**不受改名影响**，不用动。

---

## 配置 NapCat

在 NapCat 的 `config/onebot11.json` 里加一个**反向 WebSocket 客户端**：

```json
{
  "network": {
    "websocketClients": [
      {
        "name": "dsh-whale-inurqq-reverse",
        "enable": true,
        "url": "ws://127.0.0.1:6700",
        "messagePostFormat": "array",
        "reportSelfMessage": false,
        "reconnectInterval": 5000,
        "token": "<你的 access token>",
        "heartInterval": 30000
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

三个要点：

1. **`url` 指向插件**。插件默认自己监听 `127.0.0.1:6700`（`connection.mount: "own"`），
   NapCat 是主动连过来的一方。所以不用公网、不用端口映射。
2. **`messagePostFormat` 必须是 `array`**（消息段数组）。
3. **`token` 要与插件侧一致**。插件默认从 DSH 凭据 `QQ_ONEBOT_TOKEN` 读取；
   也可以用配置项 `connection.token` 直接写。

然后扫码登录：

```bash
cd <NapCat 目录>
./napcat.bat          # 控制台会打印二维码
```

---

## 配置项

```yaml
logLevel: info                    # debug | info | warn | error

connection:
  mode: reverse                   # reverse（推荐）| forward（暂未实现）
  mount: own                      # own = 插件自建服务端；dsh = 挂在 DSH 的 webServer 上
  host: 127.0.0.1                 # 只绑本机
  reversePort: 6700               # 必须与 NapCat 的 url 一致
  reversePath: /
  tokenRef: QQ_ONEBOT_TOKEN       # 从 DSH 凭据读取
  token: ''                       # 兜底值；留空且凭据也为空时表示不校验来源
  callTimeoutMs: 15000
  forwardUrl: ''                  # mode=forward 时用（暂未实现）

scope:                            # 会话白名单；空数组 = 全部允许
  groups: []
  friends: []
  blockedGroups: []
  blockedFriends: []

participation:
  groupMode: mention              # silent = 只记录不发言；mention = 被 @ 才响应；active = 自行判断
  privateMode: always

tasks:
  workspaceRoot: ''               # 必填：QQ 项目目录的父目录
  prefix: ''                      # 可选：强制任务的前缀，如 /task（优先级最高）
  chatPrefix: ''                  # 可选：强制闲聊的前缀，如 /chat（留空不启用）
  maxConcurrent: 2                # ⚠️ 只对 v2 回滚路径有意义（见 conversation.enabled）
  settleGraceMs: 3000             # 同上

ingest:
  forwardRecords: true            # 合并转发自动展开入语料（v3）
  groupArchive: true
  storeRawEvents: false

corpus:
  retainDays: 30                  # 语料保留天数，到期自动清理

conversation:                     # 常驻对接会话（默认开启）
  enabled: true                   # false = 回滚到 v2（每条任务一个新会话 + 并发上限）
  handoffAtRatio: 0.25            # 上下文用到窗口的多少比例时交班
  minTokensBetweenHandoffs: 20000 # 两次交班之间至少要增长多少 token，防止刚建好又交班
  memoryBudgetTokens: 2000        # 常驻记忆注入新会话的 token 预算（0 = 不注入）
  injectMode: context             # 注入方式；conversation.enabled=false 时不生效
  dispatchHint: true              # 在正文尾部标 [分诊: 任务]
  handoffRetainDays: 90           # 交班产物保留天数
  handoffInputChars: 120000       # 交班整理输入的字数上限
  handoffMaxTokens: 4000          # 交班整理输出的 token 上限
  fragmentMergeJaccard: 0.82      # 碎片记忆合并的相似度阈值
  fragmentAskJaccard: 0.3         # 碎片记忆追问的相似度阈值
  agingEveryGens: 10              # 每几代做一次记忆老化
  maxFragmentsPerChat: 500        # 每个会话最多保留多少条碎片

insight:                          # 定时洞察（占位，v1 未启用）
  enabled: false
  schedule: '0 22 * * *'
  pushTarget: ''

advanced:
  dedupeWindowMs: 300000          # 消息去重窗口（重连后 NapCat 可能重放）
  dedupeMaxEntries: 4096
  relayFlushMs: 2000              # 回传的合并窗口（只影响"有内容要发"的那几次）
  stateDir: ''                    # 运行时状态目录；留空用 $DSH_HOME/dsh-whale-inurqq
```

> 上面是**默认值**（由 `lib/schema.js` 定义，DSH 据此自动生成设置页）。

> ⚠️ **`conversation.enabled` 默认是 `true`**（需求定稿：默认路径就是一个常驻对接会话）。
> 设成 `false` 是**回滚开关**：整条回到 v2 的"每条任务一个新会话 + 并发上限 +
> `qq_dispatch`"行为，用于随时对照旧行为。这一条与早期"默认 false"的约定相反 ——
> 因为规则要求**默认路径**就不再新建任务会话，默认 false 等于需求在默认配置下没落地。

---

## 状态查询

插件在反向 WS 端口上暴露一个只读状态端点：

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:6700/dsh-whale-inurqq/status
```

返回连接状态、事件统计、工作区映射、回传来源判定的账目，以及任务调度与任务台账
（**只在 v2 回滚路径上非 null**）。
出问题时先看 `health.verdict`：票数不为 ok 时 `health.issues` 会直接说哪里不对
（例如"有 N 条任务会话归档失败""有 N 条任务在排队"）。

`relay` 段里有两项专门回答**规则 2 有没有生效**：

| 字段 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `provenanceDecided` | 判定过多少次"这个回合是谁发起的" |
| `skippedForeign` | 有多少个事件因为"这个回合不是插件发起的"而**整个跳过**（GUI 那一摊） |
| `trackedTurns` | 当前记着来源的会话数 |

### `alive`：它现在到底还活着吗

响应最前面是一个 `alive` 判定，形如：

```jsonc
"alive": {
  "alive": true,
  "because": [
    "QQ 通道：1 条连接、WebSocket 处于 OPEN，最近 3 秒内收到过事件帧（selfId=123456）",
    "插件自身：事件循环 120

plugins.description: Codex-style Create Workspace dialog for DeepSeek Harness: type a name and the folder is created for you, or pick a folder with a native chooser that remembers where you were.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workspace-create-dialog

[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

A **Create Workspace** dialog for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): type a name and go, or pick a folder with a chooser that finally remembers where you were.

![The Create Workspace dialog: a name field, a workspace folder row with a Choose folder button, and a New workspace location row with a Change button](docs/create-workspace.png)

## What it does

Clicking **Add workspace…** in DSH today opens the OS folder dialog immediately. This plugin replaces that with a small dialog that asks two independent questions: what is the workspace called, and where does it live. Answer the first only and it creates the folder for you; answer the second and the folder you picked *is* the workspace.

| You do | You get |
| --- | --- |
| Type a name, press **Create** | A new folder with that name is created under **New workspace location**, registered as a workspace, and a session opens in it |
| Click **Choose folder…** | The native Windows folder dialog, starting **where you left off**, not at some default |
| Choose a folder, leave the name empty | The name fills itself in from the folder's own name |
| Choose a folder, having typed a name | Your name wins — the workspace is registered, then renamed to it |
| Click **Change…** on New workspace location | Pick where name-only workspaces go from now on; the choice is saved and survives restarts |
| Cancel / Esc / click the backdrop | Nothing happens — no folder, no registration |

### The effect, before and after

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Creating `my-project` | Create the folder in Explorer first, then hunt for it in the picker | Type `my-project`. Done |
| The folder picker's starting point | The OS default, every single time | The directory you last chose |
| Where new workspaces land | Wherever you navigate to | A location you set once, visible in the dialog, changeable any time |
| Naming a workspace after its folder | Retype the folder name | Auto-filled |

## Install

### From the DSH UI (simplest)

Sidebar → **Plugins** → **Add plugin**, paste this address, click **Install**, then **Enable now**:

```text
https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog
```

That box takes a package name, a Git address, a tarball or a local absolute path. A repository URL works because this package ships a `dsh.bundle` patch — DSH checks exactly that before it installs. Restart DeepSeek Harness if the plugin does not come up.

Two things worth knowing: it downloads straight from GitHub, so GitHub has to be reachable (the China-mirror option only covers registry packages, not repository downloads); and DSH does not auto-update third-party plugins yet — upgrading means uninstall + install again.

> Already installed with `tools/install.mjs` below? Run `node tools/install.mjs --uninstall` first, so the profile does not end up with two loader rows for the same id.

### One-line prompt for your agent

If you would rather not click through it:

```text
Install the DSH plugin at https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog into my DSH and tell me when to restart.
```

### From the plugin market (once listed)

Search for **dsh-workspace-create-dialog** in [dshmarket](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) and install it in one click. The listing is [pending a PR](contrib/awesome-dsh-plugin/) to [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) (their CI requires the repository to be at least one day old); until it lands, use the routes above and below.

### Manual install from this repository

```sh
git clone https://github.com/LanFeng97/dsh-workspace-create-dialog
cd dsh-workspace-create-dialog
node tools/install.mjs
```

That copies the package into your DSH profile's `node_modules` and appends one loader line to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. It resolves your DSH home the same way the harness does — explicit config, then `$DSH_HOME`, then `~/.dsh`.

**Then restart DeepSeek Harness** (the host half is a Node module, so a config reload alone will not import it). After that, changing `lib/client.js` only needs a page refresh; changing `lib/index.js` still needs a restart.

`node tools/install.mjs --dry-run` prints what it would do without writing anything; `--uninstall` removes the package and its loader row again.

Publishing to npm is **not** required: the market installs from GitHub exactly the same way, and listing is unaffected either way.

## How it works

### It uses the official extension point, not a patch

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` declares a `single` slot where the "pick a directory" step is handed to whichever plugin fills it:

```text
sidebar.workspaces.directoryFlow              ← the sidebar's "Add workspace…"
conversation.hero.workspace.directoryFlow     ← the empty-state entry
```

The owner hands the occupant the whole interaction contract:

```ts
interface DirectoryFlowOwnerProps {
  open: boolean                     // a pick is requested
  busy: boolean                     // the owner is adopting the picked path
  onPicked: (path: string) => void  // report the directory; the owner registers it and opens a session
  onCancel: () => void
  onError: (message: string) => void
}
```

This plugin registers its own occupant into both slots at **priority -100**. A `single` slot renders the lowest-priority entry, the shipped native driver sits at `0`, so this dialog wins (two entries at the *same* priority throw, which is the official protection against ambiguity). Removing the loader line from your profile patch restores the stock behaviour exactly.

### Why the folder dialog is built here instead of reused

The desktop app opens its folder dialog from the Electron main process without a starting directory:

```js
// D:\App\DSH\resources\app.asar → lib/main.js
dialog.showOpenDialog(window, { properties: ['openDirectory', 'createDirectory'] })
```

There is no `defaultPath`, which is exactly why the chooser always starts in the same place. A plugin cannot reach that call: the DSH host is a *child process* of Electron. So `lib/pick-folder.js` opens its own `IFileDialog` — a small C# COM interop compiled and run by the **Windows PowerShell 5.1 that ships with Windows**:

- **no dependencies**: no koffi, no PowerShell 7, no native module to publish;
- compilation happens **in memory** (~120 ms per call), so there is no DLL cache to corrupt or lock;
- the one line that matters is `IFileDialog::SetFolder` — the remembered directory as the starting point;
- the dialog runs in a child process, so a native fault cannot take the host down.

The C# method declaration order must match the COM vtable (`Show=3`, `SetOptions=9`, `SetFolder=12`, `SetTitle=17`, `GetResult=20`). Getting it wrong does not error — it just silently does the wrong thing — so a self-test asserts the order.

## Where name-only workspaces are created

The **New workspace location** is resolved in this order (`lib/base-dir.js`, a pure function):

1. **What you set in the dialog** — highest priority; once you change it, it is yours;
2. **`config.baseDir`** from your profile patch — the value used at install time;
3. **The root of your default workspace** — the parent of the workspace whose directory is named `default-workspace` (a name the harness fixes, independent of UI language). New workspaces land next to it. This is the default for a fresh install;
4. **Fallback** — `<Documents>/deepseek-harness`, or `<home>/deepseek-harness` when there is no Documents folder.

The resolved value is written to the state file, so "what it was on first run" is decided once and only you change it afterwards. `config.baseDir` is a seed, not an order.

## HTTP routes

All four are loopback-guarded (loopback socket + loopback `Host` + same-origin marker; `x-forwarded-for` is never trusted) — they create directories and open windows on the host machine, so nothing off-machine may reach them.

| Route | Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/dsh-workspace-create/config` | GET | Current location + last directory |
| `/api/dsh-workspace-create/base-dir` | POST | `{"

plugins.description: 让 DeepSeek Harness 直连本地模型：兼容 OpenAI 协议（llama.cpp / LM Studio / vLLM / Ollama 的 /v1）与 Ollama 原生 API。无需登录、不消耗账号 token。
plugins.readme_text: # dsh-local-model **让 DeepSeek Harness 直连本地模型 —— 不用登录账号，也不消耗云端 token。** [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-local-model?color=blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-local-model) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-local-model)](./LICENSE) [![node](https://img.shields.io/node/v/dsh-local-model)](./package.json) [![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%5E0.2.0--rc.2-6c5ce7)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) > A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that connects the > harness to **local models** through any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or Ollama's native API. > No account sign-in, no cloud token consumption. · [English](#english) section below. --- ## 目录 - [这个插件做什么](#这个插件做什么) - [支持的本地后端](#支持的本地后端) - [安装](#安装) - [快速开始](#快速开始) - [配置项](#配置项) - [常见问题](#常见问题) - [工作原理](#工作原理) - [开发与发布](#开发与发布) - [License](#license) ## 这个插件做什么 DeepSeek Harness 默认走 DeepSeek 云端模型。本插件注册一个自定义 LLM 适配器（provider 路由 `local`）， 把 Harness 的模型请求**直接转发到你本机的推理服务**： - 🚫 **零账号依赖** —— 完全不访问 `api.deepseek.com` 或任何账号接口，不读取账号凭据，因此不产生任何云端计费。 - 🔌 **双传输协议** —— OpenAI 兼容协议 + Ollama 原生协议，两者都支持。 - 🧰 **完整工具调用** —— 正确转换 Harness 的工具调用/工具结果历史，Agent 的 bash、文件、子代理等工具都能正常用。 - 🩹 **文本工具调用兜底** —— 部分本地模型（如 `qwen2.5-coder`）会把工具调用写成纯文本 JSON，插件会自动识别并转成真正的工具调用。 - 🔍 **模型自动发现** —— 自动从本地端点拉取模型列表（Ollama `/api/tags`、OpenAI `/v1/models`）。 - ⚡ **热更新** —— 所有配置字段都是 volatile，改完无需重启。 - 🖥️ **可视化界面** —— 自带浏览器端 UI：在「设置 → 模型」的 **Local Model** 卡片里可直接 **测试连接**并列出本机可用模型；插件配置也在图形界面里完成，无需手改配置文件。 ## 支持的本地后端 | 后端 | `api` | `baseURL` | | --- | --- | --- | | **Ollama（原生，推荐）** | `ollama` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434` | | **Ollama（OpenAI 端点）** | `openai` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` | | **LM Studio** | `openai` | `http://localhost:1234/v1` | | **llama.cpp server** | `openai` | `http://localhost:8080/v1` | | **vLLM / SGLang** | `openai` | `http://localhost:8000/v1` | | **LocalAI / text-generation-webui** | `openai` | `<你的端点>/v1` | > **优先推荐直接使用本地模型**：只要后端提供 OpenAI 兼容端点，就用 `openai` 模式直连； > 用 Ollama 且想要原生 `thinking`/reasoning 支持时，用 `ollama` 模式。 ## 安装 ### 方式 A：命令行安装（推荐） ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-local-model ``` > 其中 `web` 是 profile 名；桌面版通常为 `desktop`，请按你的 profile 调整。 ### 方式 B：在 Harness 界面里安装 打开 **设置 → 插件市场**（或 **插件** 页），搜索 `dsh-local-model`，点击一键安装。 大多数插件安装后刷新页面即可生效，无需重启。 ### 方式 C：从 GitHub 安装 ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add github:/dsh-local-model ``` ### 方式 D：手动安装（无需发布） ```bash # 1. 克隆到 profile 之外任意目录 git clone https://github.com/songzhiyin/dsh-local-model.git # 2. 在 profile 里把它作为本地 link 安装 cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop pnpm add link:/绝对路径/dsh-local-model # 3. 编辑 ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json， # 在 dsh.profile.bundles 里加入 "dsh-local-model" # 4. 重启 Harness（或在插件页刷新） ``` ## 快速开始 以 Ollama 为例： ```bash # 1. 启动 Ollama 并拉取一个带 tools 能力的模型 ollama serve ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:14b # 2. 安装插件（见上一节） dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-local-model ``` 然后在 Harness 里： 1. **设置 → 模型** → 找到 **Local Model** provider，确认端点（默认 `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`）； 2. 打开任意会话，在**模型选择器**里把 provider 切到 **Local Model**，选一个模型； 3. 直接开始对话即可 —— 全程本地推理。 > 💡 跑 Agent 工具调用建议选**原生支持 function calling** 的模型（如 `qwen3-coder`、`llama3.1`、`devstral`）； > 若模型只会把工具调用写成文本（如部分 `qwen2.5-coder` 版本），插件内置的兜底也会把它转成真正的工具调用。 ## 配置项 在 **插件页 → dsh-local-model → 配置**，或 **设置 → 模型 → Local Model** 中设置： | 字段 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `api` | `"openai" \| "ollama"` | `"openai"` | 传输协议 | | `baseURL` | string | `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` | 本地端点根地址；留空按 `api` 自动选择 | | `apiKey` | string | `""` | 本地服务需要鉴权时填写（如 LM Studio 的 key） | | `defaultModel` | string | `""` | 端点无法枚举模型时的兜底模型名 | | `contextWindow` | integer | `8192` | 默认上下文窗口（token） | | `maxTokens` | integer | `2048` | 默认单次最大输出 token 数 | | `temperature` | number | `0.7` | 默认采样温度（0–2） | | `streamIdleTimeoutMs` | number | `300000` | 流式读取空闲超时（毫秒） | | `models` | array | `[]` | 静态模型清单，用于端点不支持列表查询时手动声明 | `models` 示例： ```json [ { "id": "qwen2.5-coder:14b", "name": "Qwen2.5-Coder 14B", "contextWindow": 32768, "maxTokens": 4096 } ] ``` ## 可视化界面 插件包含一个浏览器端半身（`lib/client.js`），它向「设置 → 模型」页的 provider 卡片扩展槽位 `settings.models.provider-card`（keyed，key = `dsh-local-model`）注册一张卡片： ``` ┌─ 本地模型连接测试 ─────────────────────────────────┐ │ provider: local · 名称: Local Model · 已配置: 是 │ │ 协议 [ openai（OpenAI 兼容） ▾ ] │ │ 端点 [ http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 ] [ 测试连接 ] │ │ ✅ 连接成功，发现 4 个模型 │ │ (qwen3-coder:30b) (llama3.1:8b) … │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` - 切换 `openai` / `ollama` 协议会自动填入对应的默认端点； - 「测试连接」分别请求 `/models` 或 `/api/tags`，直接显示可用模型列表； - 失败时给出可操作的提示（服务未启动 / 地址错误 / CORS 跨域）。 > 该卡片只做连通性验证；**api / baseURL / apiKey 等配置仍由上方「编辑」按钮的配置表单负责**（由插件 > 的 `Config` schema 自动渲染）。 客户端半身是**手写的 Lazy-CJS bundle**（`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`）， 只依赖平台模块表里的 `react`，不需要任何打包步骤、也不需要 `dsh.client.external`。 ## 常见问题 **Q：模型列表是空的？** 确认本地服务已启动且 `baseURL` 正确。若端点不支持 `/models`（或 `/api/tags`），请在 `models` 里手动声明。 **Q：报 `AUTH` 错误？** 说明本地服务需要鉴权，把 key 填进 `apiKey`。 **Q：模型把工具调用当纯文本吐出来（`{"name":"skill","arguments":{...}}`）？** 这是该模型的工具调用能力问题，不是插件问题。插件已内置**文本工具调用兜底**：会识别 `{...}` JSON、 `...`、` ```json {...} ``` ` 三种写法，并在工具名匹配时自动转成真正的工具调用。 如果仍不稳定，建议换用原生支持 function calling 的模型。 **Q：reasoning / 思考内容怎么显示？** `openai` 模式读取 `reasoning_content`，`ollama` 模式读取 `thinking`，都会映射为 Harness 的 reasoning 块。 **Q：长对话被截断？** 多数本地服务有自己的上下文上限（Ollama 默认 `num_ctx=4096`）。可以用环境变量放宽，例如 `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768 ollama serve`，或改用长上下文模型（如 `devstral`）。 **Q：「测试连接」报 `Failed to fetch`，但命令行 `curl` 明明能通？** 这是 **`localhost` 的 IPv6 陷阱**：在部分环境下 `localhost` 会先解析到 IPv6 `::1`， 而 Ollama 等本地服务通常只监听 IPv4 `127.0.0.1`，于是浏览器直连失败。 本插件已内置两道防护： 1. **探测默认走宿主进程**（`ctx.remote.llm.discoverModels()`）——由 Node 侧发起请求， 完全绕开浏览器的 CORS / IPv6 / Electron 网络策略； 2. 默认地址一律用 **`127.0.0.1`** 而不是 `localhost`，并对回环地址做 `localhost ⇄ 127.0.0.1` 的自动兜底重试。 如果你在配置里手写了 `localhost`，建议改成 `127.0.0.1`。 ## 工作原理 插件通过 `ctx.llm.registerAdapter(["local"], adapter)` 注册一个 `LlmAdapter`，把 Harness 的 `GenerateOptions` 翻译成目标协议的请求，再把流式响应翻译回 Harness 的 `StreamChunk` （`block-start` / `text-delta` / `reasoning-delta` / `tool-call-delta` / `block-end` / `usage` / `finish`）。 - 不访问任何 DeepSeek 云端端点； - 不读取账号凭据，因此不产生云端 token 消耗； - 文件引用与图片由 Harness 运行时自动投影为文本句柄（文本模型），适配器只需处理文本与工具调用。 ## 开发与发布 ```bash git clone https://github.com/songzhiyin/dsh-local-model.git cd dsh-local-model # 本地 link 到你的 DSH profile 做开发（改代码即时生效） cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop pnpm add link:/绝对路径/dsh-local-model ``` 发布到 npm： ```bash npm publish # publishConfig.access 已设为 public ``` 上架插件市场（可选，让更多人发现）： 向 [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) 仓库提交一个 PR， 加入一条注册表条目（`name` / `owner` / `url` / `category` / `description` / `npm` / `install` / `added`）， 市场与官网会自动收录。 ## License [MIT](./LICENSE) --- ## English **Connect DeepSeek Harness to local models — no account sign-in, no cloud token usage.** `dsh-local-model` registers a `local` LLM adapter that routes every model call to your own machine: - **Zero account dependency** — never touches `api.deepseek.com` or any account endpoint. - **Two transports** — OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions`, and Ollama's native `/api/chat` (NDJSON, with `thinking` support). - **Full tool calling** — converts Harness tool-call / tool-result history correctly, plus a fallback that recovers tool calls some local models emit as plain-text JSON. - **Model discovery** — pulls the model list from `GET /models` or `GET /api/tags`. - **Visual configuration** — configure it from the Harness **Plugins** page or **Settings → Models**; no config file editing. ### Install ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-local-model ``` Or search for `dsh-local-model` in **Settings → Plugin Market** inside Harness. ### Quick start (Ollama) ```bash ollama serve ollama pull qwen3-coder # any tool-capable model works dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-local-model ``` Then, inside Harness: **Settings → Models** confirms the **Local Model** provider (default endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`), and you pick it from the session's model selector.

plugins.description: 最小权限检查：容器 root/privileged、IAM 通配、CORS 全开、令牌申请 admin。
plugins.readme_text:
# @deepwhale-cn/dsh-least-privilege

[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/feely0208/dsh-least-privilege)


**关键词**：最小权限 · 权限过宽 · 权限管理 · 容器 root · IAM · CORS · 访问控制 · 权限最小化 · 特权容器
**Keywords**: least privilege · over-permission · container root · IAM wildcard · CORS · access control
**最小权限检查** —— 容器跑 root、IAM 通配、CORS 全开、令牌申请 admin。

## 不装它会怎样

你的部署里有这么一段：

```yaml
services:
  app:
    privileged: true
```

当时是为了让容器能访问某个设备，后来那个需求没了，**但这行留下了**。

哪天应用出了个漏洞，攻击者进到容器里 —— 而因为 `privileged`，
他拿到的几乎是**宿主机**。

**权限过宽是入侵的放大器**，而且它**没有任何症状** —— 系统照常跑，
直到出事那天你才发现那把钥匙能开所有的门。

## 它查什么

| 级别 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 🔴 高 | 容器跑 root / `--privileged` · IAM `Action: *` |
| 🟡 中 | CORS 允许所有来源 · 令牌申请 admin/全量 scope |

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @deepwhale-cn/dsh-least-privilege
# 或纯 CLI
npx @deepwhale-cn/dsh-least-privilege
```

## 用法

```bash
dsh-least-privilege --demo
dsh-least-privilege --list-rules
dsh-least-privilege --html r.html
```

![dsh-least-privilege 检查报告示例](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-least-privilege/report.png)

![dsh-least-privilege 演示模式输出](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-least-privilege/demo.png)

![dsh-least-privilege 规则与依据](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-least-privilege/rules.png)

## 边界

- **只查「明显过宽」的写法** —— 权限偏大但没用通配符的，需要人工评审。
- **不解析云厂商实际生效策略** —— IAM 有继承/条件/边界，只看仓库里字面写的。
- **Dockerfile 可能多阶段** —— builder 阶段的 `USER root` 通常无害，需你判断。
- 与 [dsh-data-scan](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-scan) 分工：那个查数据，这个查**访问数据的权限**。

本插件是一个工具。使用者必须遵守所在地区法律法规，**对使用本项目造成的任何后果自行承担责任。**

---

## 深鲸网安守护系列（共 38 个）

plugins.description: 列出并删除 DSH 已归档会话：默认移入回收站可恢复，带二次确认与日志归属校验。
plugins.readme_text:
## dsh-delete-archived-session
一个 DSH 插件：**列出并删除已归档的会话**。
DSH 本身只有「归档」和「取消归档」两个操作。**归档只是把会话藏起来，日志永远留在磁盘上**，官方没有任何办法把那块空间收回来。
### 安全设计

删会话就是把聊天记录销毁掉，所以这个插件刻意做得很保守。

1.只删已归档的。

2.必须明确确认。

3.必须先证明归属。

4.不跑出根目录。

5.默认可以恢复。

6.顺手清掉归档记录。

7.DSH不崩。

### 安装

这是一个标准的 DSH 插件包：`package.json` 里声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`，`cordis.patch.yml` 负责插入一行。

**方法一（推荐）**：在对话里说一句「把这个插件装上」，让 AI 调用插件管理器安装。

**方法二**：自己手动加。在 profile 的 `package.json` 里加依赖并登记 bundle：

```json
{
  "dependencies": { "dsh-delete-archived-session": "file:./dsh-delete-archived-session" },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["dsh-delete-archived-session"] } }
}
```

装好后需要重启 DSH 才生效。

### 配置

插件**不导入 Node 标准库以外的任何东西**——它注册的是朴素的工具/命令描述对象，也不接受 schemastery 的 `Config`。这样做是为了不管 profile 怎么提升 DSH 自身的依赖，它都能挂载成功。

配置因此走环境变量：

| 环境变量 | 默认值 | 含义 |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_DELETE_ARCHIVED_SESSIONS_ROOT` | `$DSH_HOME/sessions` | 要操作的会话根目录 |
| `DSH_DELETE_ARCHIVED_SESSIONS_TRASH` | `<根目录>/../.deleted-sessions` | 删除时移入的回收站 |
| `DSH_DELETE_ARCHIVED_SESSIONS_PERMANENT` | 不设（允许永久删除） | 设为 `0`、`false` 或 `no` 则禁止永久删除，强制走可恢复路径 |

`$DSH_HOME` 的读取方式和 DSH 本身一致：先看 `$DSH_HOME`，没有就用 `~/.dsh`。

plugins.description: DSH plugin: give the agent a mouth through the ai-ball floating orb (speak, mood, panel, listen).
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-ai-ball

> 给 agent 一张嘴：让它通过 [ai-ball](https://github.com/Hyfwdnmd666/ai-ball) 那颗悬浮球说话、做表情、听你打字。

ai-ball 是一个 Windows 悬浮球 —— 它把自己追加到 `monologue.log` 的文字逐字"说"出来、
按 `status.json` 里的 mood 变色、把你打进输入框的话追加到 `input.log`。
**球本身是哑的，它只认文件。**

所以这个插件很薄：它不去操作球的窗口，也不 spawn Python，**它只写球已经在看的那些文件**。
这也是为什么任何进程都能当球的"大脑"。

## 你需要什么

1. **ai-ball 本体**（一个 Python 3.10+ 的目录，里面有 `ball.py`）
2. 把它跑起来（双击 `start.bat`，或 `python ball.py`）

插件本身不包含球，也不会替你安装它。

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-ai-ball
```

或者从市场里装。

## 配置

挂在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里：

```yaml
- id: dsh-ai-ball
  name: dsh-ai-ball
  config:
    ballDir: C:\tools\ai-ball        # 必填：放着 ball.py 的那个目录
    startCommand: C:\tools\ai-ball\start.bat   # 可选：ball_launch 用
    cps: 50                          # 可选：球的打字速度，用来估算 wait
    heartbeatMs: 3000                # 可选：心跳间隔，必须小于球那边的 stale_s
    files:                           # 可选：和球自己的 config.json 对齐
      monologue: monologue.log
      input: input.log
      status: status.json
```

也可以走环境变量 `AIBALL_DIR` / `AIBALL_START`。

**`ballDir` 故意没有默认值。** 猜别人把球解压到哪儿了，正是插件往错目录里写文件的方式 ——
所以它宁可报一个说清楚哪里不对的错。

## 六个工具

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `ball_say` | 说话。追加到 `monologue.log`，球逐字念出来。`clear=true` 先清屏 |
| `ball_mood` | 改球的脸：`idle` / `thinking` / `nervous` / `smug` / `broken` |
| `ball_panel` | 显示 / 收起独白面板 |
| `ball_listen` | 读你在球里打的字（`input.log`），只返回新的 |
| `ball_status` | 报告接线情况：文件大小、最后说了什么、心跳多旧、有没有在心跳 |
| `ball_launch` | 按配置的 `startCommand` 把球拉起来 |

## 两个会让你浪费一下午的坑

### 1. 心跳不是可选项 —— 插件会自己接管它

球把**过期的心跳**读成"大脑死了"并渲染成灰色，而那会**盖掉 mood**。

所以 `ball_mood` 不只是写一次 mood：它同时启动一个心跳，**在插件加载期间一直刷**。
这有两个后果：

- 第一次调 `ball_mood` 之后，球就再也不会因为你没在做事而变灰了（这是对的：
  插件活着 = harness 活着）
- 插件被卸载/重载时心跳会停（挂在 cordis 的 dispose 上，不会泄漏定时器）

一个只写一次 `mood`、不管心跳的实现，看起来像成功了，然后 20 秒后静默失效。

### 2. 如果 `brain.py` 在跑，它每三秒会把你的 mood 踩回 `idle`

`brain.py` 每隔几秒重写整个 `status.json`（心跳是它的）。
两个写者抢同一个文件，后写的赢。

想自己拥有球的脸，在 `brain.json` 里设：

```json
{ "write_mood": false }
```

那样它只刷心跳，文件里现有的 `mood` 原样保留 —— 两个写者就能共存了。

### 3. `ball_panel` 为什么带一个序号

`status.json` 里的 `panel` **不是"当前该是什么状态"，是一条命令**，`panel_seq` 是它的序号。
球只在**序号变化**时动一次。

不这么做的话，插件每几秒重写一次文件，就等于和你抢面板开关：
你收起面板，它下一拍又打开。

带序号之后：

- 你手动开关面板**一直算数**（插件没改变主意，序号没变）
- 插件改变主意时把序号加一，球再执行一次
- **每次调 `ball_panel` 都是新请求**（序号加一），所以"你关掉了，我要它再显示"
  是有效的，不会变成空操作

（球那边没有 `panel_seq` 的 `panel` 一律不执行 —— 没有序号就无法区分"你刚关掉"和
"它一直这么说"，照做就是抢开关。）

## `ball_listen` 为什么不会切坏中文

读游标按**字节**记，而且只推进到**最后一个换行**。

写入方可能被撞见写到一半：游标如果按字符算、或者用替换字符解码尾部，
那半个 UTF-8 序列会变成 U+FFFD **并且永久留在游标后面** —— 内容就再也读不出来了。
停在最后一个换行，残缺的尾巴下次会重新读一遍，这是简单正确的做法。

（同一个 bug、同一个修法，ai-ball 的 Python 侧也有一份。）

## 它不做的事

- **不判断球在不在跑。** `ball_status` 报的是文件状态，不是窗口状态 —— 严格来说，一个没在跑的球
  和一个在跑但没人写的球，看起来是一样的。
- **不会只启动一颗球。** `ball_launch` 是只写的，重复调用会得到两颗球。
- **不渲染 Markdown。** 球是嘴，不是文档。`**强调**` 会原样显示出来。
- **不会替你记住要开面板。** `ball_say` 不会自动显示面板 —— 面板收着的时候它照样写成功，
  只是没人看得见。要保证被看到，先 `ball_panel(true)`。

## 许可

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: DSH File Converter: local file conversion across 20 tool chains and 1000+ format pairs — convert files, query the format matrix, and check converter availability via model tools.  DSH 文件格式转换插件：跨 20 个转换器、覆盖 1000+ 格式对，以模型工具提供本地文件转换、格式矩阵查询与转换器可用性检测
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-converter

[**English**](README.md) | [中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A **file conversion plugin for DSH (DeepSeek Harness)**. It provides a conversion engine
that covers **20 tool chains / 1000+ format pairs**
(images / audio-video / documents / e-books / 3D / spreadsheets ...) and runs entirely through
external CLIs (`ffmpeg`, `pandoc`, `libreoffice`, `imagemagick`, `vips`, `calibre`, ...) or pure JS (`vcf`),
exposed to the model as tools.

DSH framework docs: <https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/develop/basic/>

## 1. Tools

| Tool                | Purpose                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `convert_file`      | Convert a local file: `{ inputPath, to, from?, outputPath?, converter? }`. Output defaults to the input directory (same name, new extension). Unsupported pairs return the list of available targets; missing converter returns the install command |
| `list_conversions`  | Query the format matrix: pass `from` to get that format's convertible targets (grouped by converter); omit it for a full category overview             |
| `check_converters`  | Detect which converter CLIs are available on this machine (with version numbers)                                                                        |

## 2. Installation

### From npm / GitHub

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-converter                        # install from npm
dsh plugin --profile web add github:ai-tool-labs/dsh-converter    # or from GitHub
# Desktop: open the "Plugins" panel in the sidebar → click "Add Plugin" → type "dsh-converter" → Install
# Restart harness after installing to take effect (Desktop: restart the App; Web: restart dsh web)
```

### From source (developer)

```bash
# 1) Build
pnpm install && pnpm --filter dsh-converter build

# 2) Install into a profile (example: web profile)
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-plugins/packages/dsh-converter
```

### Enable in the profile

Append the following to `<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` (the shipped `cordis.patch.yml` shows all
options, commented out):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: file-converter
      name: dsh-converter
      config:
        enableTools: true
        enableSkill: true
        maxFileSizeMb: 500      # per-file size limit (default 500MB, matches the Web version)
        timeoutMs: 300000       # external CLI timeout (default 5 minutes)
```

## 3. Converter dependencies

`check_converters` tells you which converters are missing; install commands per platform:

| Converter   | Purpose                 | macOS                             | Ubuntu                       | Windows                  |
| ----------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| ffmpeg      | Audio / video / GIF     | `brew install ffmpeg`             | `apt install ffmpeg`         | `choco install ffmpeg`   |
| pandoc      | Universal doc conversion| `brew install pandoc`             | `apt install pandoc`         | `choco install pandoc`   |
| libreoffice | Office / PDF            | `brew install --cask libreoffice` | `apt install libreoffice`    | `choco install libreoffice` |
| imagemagick | Images                  | `brew install imagemagick`        | `apt install imagemagick`    | `choco install imagemagick` |
| vips        | Images (high-perf)      | `brew install vips`               | `apt install libvips-tools`  | `choco install vips`     |
| calibre     | E-books                 | `brew install --cask calibre`     | `apt install calibre`        | `choco install calibre`  |
| inkscape    | Vector graphics         | `brew install --cask inkscape`    | `apt install inkscape`       | `choco install inkscape` |
| xelatex     | LaTeX → PDF             | `brew install --cask mactex`      | `apt install texlive-xetex`  | install MiKTeX           |
| vcf         | Contacts vcf → csv      | ✅ pure JS, no install            | ✅                            | ✅                       |

See `src/engine/installCommands.ts` for the full list (all 20 tool chains, per-platform commands).

## 4. Architecture

```
src/index.ts          —— entry: Config / inject / apply
src/tools.ts          —— convert_file / list_conversions / check_converters
src/skills.ts         —— file-conversion skill (teaches the model how to use it)
src/engine/           —— ported conversion engine (logic identical to the original project)
  ├── registry.ts           —— format-matrix pure data + query functions (no Node deps)
  ├── fileTypeCategories.ts —— extension → category (pure data)
  ├── normalizeFiletype.ts  —— format alias normalization (jfif→jpeg, md→markdown, ...)
  ├── main.ts               —— mainConverter: auto-select converter + path/Buffer I/O
  └── <converter>.ts        —— 20 converters (ffmpeg/pandoc/vips/vcf/...)
```

### Key differences from the Web version

1. **File I/O**: input and output are local paths (the Web version uses HTTP upload + OSS storage);
2. **Timeout & cancellation**: injected through the engine's `execFileOverride` extension point —
   external CLI timeouts (`timeoutMs` config) auto-kill, and cancellation of the tool call
   (`exec.signal`) terminates the child process immediately without leaving zombies;
3. **Self-healing errors**: unsupported pairs return `availableTargets`, missing converters return
   install commands — the model can self-correct instead of failing repeatedly;
4. **Diagnosable**: `check_converters` exposes CLI availability to the model.

### Engine notes

- The engine is written in TypeScript with **zero third-party dependencies** (Node built-ins only):
  - imports use relative paths;
  - `main.ts` is the main converter and exposes an `execFileOverride` extension point (used for timeout / cancellation);
  - `detectOS()` is implemented for a Node environment (rather than browser UA detection).
- Because the engine has no runtime dependencies, it is self-contained and easy to maintain.

## 5. Development

```bash
pnpm --filter dsh-converter typecheck   # type check
pnpm --filter dsh-converter build       # tsc → build/
pnpm --filter dsh-converter smoke       # smoke test:
                                                   #   vcf→csv (pure JS) real conversion,
                                                   #   unsupported-format error hints,
                                                   #   format-matrix query, unload cleanup
```

plugins.description: DSH Tauri plugin: forward a task notification to email (SMTP) or pushplus when a task stops abnormally or completes, and only while the window is not in front of you.
plugins.readme_text:
[![dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-yes-4b6bfb)](https://github.com/iuuuuuuuu/dsh-tauri-notify-webhook)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2ea44f)](./LICENSE)
[![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.15-339933)](https://nodejs.org)

# dsh-tauri-notify-webhook

**English** · [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md)

Forward a DSH desktop task notification to **email (SMTP)** or **pushplus** — when a task
stops abnormally or completes, and only while the window is not in front of you.

## The problem this solves

The desktop shell already shows a toast when a turn ends, and it is easy to miss for a
reason worth stating precisely:

- A toast is a system notification. If the window is in front of you, you were already
  watching the answer stream in — the toast is noise. If you walked away, the toast is
  gone by the time you come back, and nothing remains on screen.
- The interesting endings are not equally interesting. A turn that ran to the end needs no
  attention. A turn that **errored, was aborted, hit the token ceiling or was blocked** does.
- The host keeps only the **latest** `turn/end` per session, so a finished session leaves no
  queue to read later. Once you were away for that moment, the information is simply gone.

This plugin moves the notification off the screen and onto a channel that keeps history,
and it fires only for the two endings you would actually act on.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:iuuuuuuuu/dsh-tauri-notify-webhook
```

The same spec works in the GUI plugin panel (**设置 → 插件 → 安装**), which accepts any npm
spec. For a local checkout, install the directory instead:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add link:D:/path/to/dsh-tauri-notify-webhook
```

There is no build step at install time: `dist/` is committed. This is deliberate — the
desktop profile installs plugins as packages, and a package that has to be compiled after
installation would need a toolchain the profile does not have.

**Restart DSH.** This is required, not optional: the harness keeps loaded plugin modules in
its loader cache, and `hmr.root` defaults to `[]`, so a newly installed plugin does not take
effect in a running host.

## Use

Open **设置 → 任务推送**, pick a channel, fill in its fields, press **发送测试**, then
**保存**. The test button only becomes available once the form differs from what is saved,
so a successful test always describes exactly the values you are about to store.

| Channel | What it needs |
| --- | --- |
| 邮件 (SMTP) | SMTP host, port, security, from, to; username and password are optional for relays that accept anonymous mail |
| pushplus | A token from [pushplus.plus](https://www.pushplus.plus); pushes go straight to the official `/send` endpoint |
| 关闭 | Nothing is sent. This is the default |

## What it does

### Two triggers

| Trigger | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| 任务完成 | The turn ended with reason `completed` |
| 任务异常停止 | The turn ended any other way — `aborted`, `error`, `blocked`, `max-tokens`, `interrupted`, `forked` |

Both are on by default and are switched independently. Sub-agent sessions are skipped: they
are driven by their parent, so they would otherwise produce a burst of pushes for one task.

### Only while you are away

A push is sent only when `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`. The Tauri shell patches
`document.hidden` to the real window focus state, so this is "the window is not in front of
you" rather than "the tab is in the background". While you are watching the session, the
plugin stays silent.

### How one push is decided

The client cannot read a turn's ending reason, so the decision takes two round trips:

1. The session list flips a session from `running: true` to `false` — that edge is the only
   thing watched, so a session that was already finished when the plugin loaded is never
   back-filled.
2. After a 250 ms settle window (a turn can flicker its running flag), the client asks
   `GET /turn-end?sessionId=…` for the reason the host recorded.
3. If the session is still stopped and has not stopped again in the meantime, the client
   posts `POST /delivery`. The host re-reads the settings at that moment and sends.

Every step re-checks that the plugin is still loaded, so a reload mid-flight cannot deliver
a stale push.

## Where your credentials live

Settings are stored on this machine only, at `$DSH_HOME/notify-webhook/settings`
(`DSH_HOME` defaults to `~/.dsh`). The file is written through the shell's atomic-write
helper, so a crash mid-save cannot leave a truncated config. Nothing is uploaded anywhere
except the channel you configure.

The host routes are loopback-only, and every mutating request must also be same-origin;
a browser page on another origin cannot read your settings or make the plugin send mail.

## Requirements

* The DSH **desktop (Tauri)** shell — this plugin is a client of the shell's `dsh-tauri`
  and `dsh-tauri-ui` runtime plugins, and of the `settings.section` slot, so it does not
  apply to a browser-only profile.
* Node.js ≥ 22.15.0.
* For email: an SMTP server you can send through. For pushplus: a token.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
pnpm lint        # eslint .
pnpm test        # vitest run
pnpm build       # tsdown -> dist/index.js, dist/index.d.ts, dist/client.cjs
```

CI runs the same four gates on Node 22 and 24, and then asserts that `dist/` is up to date
(`git diff --exit-code -- dist`) — if you change `src/`, commit the rebuilt `dist/` with it.

`compat/` holds local stand-ins for the two modules the shell injects at runtime
(`dsh-tauri`, `dsh-tauri/client`, `dsh-tauri-ui/client`). They exist so that `tsc` and the
unit tests can run outside the desktop app; `tsdown` marks those specifiers external, so
none of this code reaches `dist/`.

## License

MIT

[![powered by dsh](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered_by-dsh-4D6BFE?style=flat-square&logo=deepseek&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)

---
description: "DSH plugin: pool several local inference endpoints into one compute pool and spread delegated subagents across them, with per-endpoint admission control."
kind: "package-bundle"
---

# Local compute pool

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A **DeepSeek Harness plugin** that pools several local inference endpoints into one compute pool:
delegated subagents are spread across the machines by load, every endpoint has its own concurrency
gate and queue, a failing endpoint is parked and the next attempt fails over — and when no local
endpoint is usable, children keep the route the harness resolved.

* Package: `dsh-local-compute-pool` · Card title: **Local compute pool** / 本地算力池
* Distribution: a **plain directory bundle** (not an npm package) — clone this repository and install
  it by absolute path, as described below
* License: MIT

---

## What it solves

A locally served model has three hard limits, and every mechanism here maps to one of them:

| Reality of local inference | What the plugin does |
| --- | --- |
| VRAM/RAM is limited — usually one conversation at a time | A per-endpoint **concurrency gate** (default 1): at most `concurrency` requests at once, the rest queue (with a depth limit and a timeout) |
| Context caching is weak | Each subagent is **pinned to one machine for its whole life**, so the prompt prefix and the tool-call dialect stay stable |
| Parallel requests are handled poorly | The `least-busy` strategy spreads subagents across machines instead of stacking them behind one |

The point is not "going faster" — it is **turning "start several subagents" from unusable into usable**
on local models: a local server that receives two concurrent requests often does not run each at half
speed, it times out on both or blows up its VRAM.

---

## You may be stuck exactly here

Picture this: you own a few good GPUs. Running an LLM under a framework such as
[Strata](https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20261005-strata-local-ai) or
[NInfer](https://github.com/natpate/ninfer-windows) gives you speed and quality you are happy with.
You are not short of computers — but a consumer motherboard usually has only two PCIe slots, so you
cannot fit them all into one machine, and therefore cannot make them work on one task **at the same
time**.

The bottleneck was never raw compute. It is that the compute sits in several separate computers,
each fighting alone.

**Local compute pool was written for exactly that.** It lets models on different computers take part
in the same task as delegated subagents: the main agent splits the work, the plugin places the
resulting subagents on the available machines to run in parallel, and the results are gathered back.

This is how I use it: one machine with a 5090 and one with dual 4080S cards, each running Qwen 3.8
Flash Next at roughly 100 tok/s. With this plugin, two subagents of the same task land on the two
machines and proceed at once — **about 200 tok/s of combined effective throughput**, as if the two
computers had been soldered into the single machine your slots could not hold.

> To be precise: this does not make a **single generation** faster — autoregressive decoding cannot
> add two streams of tokens together. It makes **several subagents inside one task truly parallel**,
> so total throughput stacks.

## The two lists on the settings page

The settings page is built around two lists with clearly separate jobs:

1. **Trigger whitelist** — marks **which models may enable this plugin**. Only when a task's own model
   runs on a whitelisted provider are its subagents handed to the local pool; tasks that are not ticked
   are untouched and keep the route the harness resolved.
2. **Subagent model pool** — lists **which machines/endpoints offer compute**. Each endpoint gets its
   own concurrency, and the plugin spreads subagents across them by load.

---

## Requirements

* DeepSeek Harness desktop (developed and verified on `0.2.0-rc.2`).
* At least one local OpenAI-compatible provider already configured in `llm-pi-ai` (for example
  `local` → `http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1`). The plugin sends no HTTP of its own and adds no provider:
  it only decides *who* and queues.

## Install

Two steps, and that is all: **no npm, no build step, no dependencies.** This repository is a plain
directory bundle — cloning it gives you everything the plugin needs.

Clone this repository:

```
git clone https://github.com/suanlv/dsh-local-compute-pool.git
```

Then install the `plugin` directory by its **absolute path**:

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle
                target: <cloned repo>\plugin
```

> Not on npm, on purpose: publishing would add a registry account and a republish-on-every-change
> ritual, in exchange for saving one `git clone`. See [docs/DESIGN.en.md](docs/DESIGN.en.md).

Afterwards:

* the package joins the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, and this repository's `plugin/cordis.patch.yml`
  is inserted as one patch layer for the plugin row;
* a freshly installed bundle activates live; if it reports `restart-required`, restart the desktop app;
* later edits to `cordis.patch.yml`'s `config` are reloaded by HMR, while **editing JavaScript
  (`index.js` / `lib/*` / `client.js`) needs a restart** (the browser half only needs a page refresh).

Remove it with `plugin_manager action: remove_bundle target: dsh-local-compute-pool`.

## First run

1. **Add endpoints**: sidebar **Plugins** → card **Local compute pool** → *Subagent model pool* →
   *+ Add a local endpoint*. Pick the `provider` from the live directory, choose `auto` (the first
   model that provider advertises) or an exact id, and set `concurrency` to how many requests that
   machine serves at once (1 for a single-session local server).
   **The shipped endpoint list is empty**: a default pointing at a service that does not exist on
   someone else's machine can only fail, so none is preset.
2. **Decide who may use local compute**: tick providers in the *Trigger whitelist*. Only tasks whose
   own model runs on those providers hand their subagents to the local pool; an empty whitelist means
   "no restriction". The number beside each entry is that task's subagent cap: it is written into the
   task's prompt and **enforced** at the stream gate (counted per task, across machines).
3. **Verify**: start two subagents in one message — they should land on different endpoints. Or have
   the model call the `local_pool` tool to see in-flight / queued / parked counts per machine, how
   many slots a task holds for itself, and each task's subagent budget.

## Known boundaries (read this before filing an issue)

* **Subagents only.** With the default `applyTo: children` the main agent keeps its own model. Setting
  it to `all` moves the main agent's **whole conversation** onto a local model, and tool calling then
  depends on that model.
* **It sends no HTTP and does not retry.** Requests go through the provider you configured in
  `llm-pi-ai`; retries belong to `dsh-llm-retry`. The plugin simply re-picks an endpoint each time a
  retry passes through `agent/request` — which is exactly why a failure can move to another machine.
* **It does not know about "devices", only provider ids.** Every endpoint is a `127.0.0.1`-style
  address; a remote machine is reached through port forwarding or a tunnel. It **cannot tell
  "two ports on one machine" from "two machines"**, and has no device discovery, remote transport,
  cluster membership or authentication.
* **No cross-machine cooperation**: no session migration, no shared cache, no distributed state. Each
  subagent's world is the machine it is pinned to.
* **Not a general-purpose load balancer**: the decision unit is a subagent, not a request.
* `concurrency` is a value you declare; the plugin cannot probe what the server really supports.
  Setting it too high will crush the local server.

## Configuration

The full field reference is in [plugin/README.md](plugin/README.md) (Chinese) and
[plugin/README.en.md](plugin/README.en.md) (English). Every option in the shipped
`plugin/cordis.patch.yml` carries a comment.

# @deepwhale-cn/dsh-pipia

**个人信息保护影响评估** —— 查是否按个保法 55 条做了评估、56 条留存三年。

## 不装它会怎样

你的代码里有人脸核身：

```js
const faceId = await extractFace(imageBase64);
await push(userId, { userInfo: await getUser(userId), faceId });
```

**业务上没问题。法律上踩了第 55 条：**

> **《个人信息保护法》第五十五条**
> 处理**敏感个人信息**、利用个人信息进行自动化决策、
> 委托处理 / 向他人提供 / 公开个人信息、向境外提供个人信息
> —— **应当事前进行个人信息保护影响评估，并对处理情况进行记录**

> **第五十六条**
> 评估报告和处理情况记录应当**至少保存三年**。

**这条是「必须做」，不是「建议做」。** 而且监管检查时会**直接要求出示**。

## 关键词
**关键词**：个人信息保护影响评估 · 影响评估 · PIPIA · DPIA · 敏感个人信息 · 合规评估 · 评估报告 · 保存三年
**Keywords**: PIPIA · DPIA · privacy impact assessment · PIPL · sensitive personal information

## 它查什么

| 级别 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 🔴 高 | 处理**敏感个人信息**但找不到评估 | 处理**对外提供**但找不到评估 |
| 🟡 中 | 仓库里找不到任何评估记录 | |
| 🟢 低 | 提到了评估但**没写保存期限**（56 条要求三年）| |

## 两条规则是「条件适用」的

`PIPIA-SENSITIVE-NO-ASSESS` 和 `PIPIA-THIRD-PARTY-NO-ASSESS` **只在项目确实有相应处理活动时才跑**。
没有敏感信息的项目跑这两条就是误报 —— 引擎的条件规则能力（`check.when`）。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @deepwhale-cn/dsh-pipia
# 或纯 CLI
npx @deepwhale-cn/dsh-pipia
```

![dsh-pipia 检查报告示例](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-pipia/report.png)

![dsh-pipia 演示模式输出](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-pipia/demo.png)

![dsh-pipia 规则与依据](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-pipia/rules.png)

## 用法

```bash
dsh-pipia --demo
dsh-pipia --list-rules
dsh-pipia --html r.html
```

## 边界

- **不会替你写评估报告** —— 它只发现「你处理了这些活动，但找不到评估痕迹」。
- **评估通常在仓库外**（法务文档、内部系统）—— 报出来是提示你确认，不是断定你没做。
- **敏感信息靠字段/关键词识别** —— 自定义命名会漏。
- **不做「必要性」判断** —— 该项处理是否属于必须评估的情形，最终是法律判断。
- 与 [dsh-cn-data-export](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-data-export) 分工：
  那个查**数据出境**，这个查**评估流程**（出境也是必须评估的情形之一）。

本插件是一个工具。使用者必须遵守所在地区法律法规，**对使用本项目造成的任何后果自行承担责任。**

---

## 深鲸网安守护系列（共 38 个）

> 一个插件做一件事。**安全问题是链式的** —— 配套用才完整。

**国内合规**（12）｜ [等保对照](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-mlps) · [日志留存](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-log-retention) · [备案公示](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-filing) · [用户同意](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-consent-guard) · [个人信息权利](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-rights) · [未成年人保护](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-minor-guard) · [影响评估](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-pipia) · [数据分类分级](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-classify) · [算法备案](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-algorithm-filing) · [数据出境](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-data-export) · [国密合规](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-crypto) · [AI 内容标识](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-ai-labeling)

**AI 与 Agent 治理**（6）｜ [AI 输出信任](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-ai-output-trust) · [外部内容信任](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-content-trust) · [MCP 安全](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-mcp-audit) · [Agent 权限](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-agent-scope) · [策略核对](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-agent-policy) · [可疑指令](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-phishing-guard)

# @guojinpeng/dsh-cost-meter

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

This plugin shows estimated session and turn costs in DSH.
Use DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 or later.
Tests use DSH 0.2.0-rc.2.

![Session and turn cost overview](docs/images/overview.png)

## Install

1. Install the npm package:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add -w @guojinpeng/dsh-cost-meter
```

2. Restart DSH.
3. Open **Plugins**.
4. Select **@guojinpeng/dsh-cost-meter** to change prices.

Replace `web` with your profile name.
If you used the old unscoped package, disable it before you install this package.

Install published versions from npm. npm provides the built package.
GitHub contains the source code and release notes.

## Features

- Shows session and completed-turn cost estimates. The session chip sits in the composer, and the turn chip follows the official turn usage pill, with the clock last. Both use the price tag icon.
- Adds a **Cost statistics** entry to the sidebar **Plugins** area. Select it to open the cost overview page.
- Shows a short initialization message when model prices are not ready.
- Groups the details by peak price, off-peak price and fixed price. Hides price rows that cost zero and shows no peak or off-peak token counts.
- The session panel groups the four prices by peak, off-peak and fixed price, then lists each model's group sums. The turn panel lists the four prices of every group for each model.
- Each price has an info button: hover it to see the calculation formula for that price. The popover closes when the pointer leaves.
- Groups used models by provider. The list comes from DSH session history and models declared in the configuration.
- Supports separate prices for each full `provider/model` name.
- Selects models.dev, openrouter.ai or api.deepinfra.com as the price source.
- Initializes new model prices from the selected source's local cache. Uses zero if there is no matching price.
- Downloads model prices only when you select **Sync prices**. The source controls, the Sync prices button and the sync report stay above the model rates table.
- Syncs only configured models. The sync result is staged in the draft and written to the configuration when you select **Save**.
- Matches source prices by model ID. models.dev prefers manufacturer prices; OpenRouter and DeepInfra supply their own platform prices. Keeps existing prices if matching is unclear.
- Keeps existing prices when the source cannot supply a supported rate.
- Supports USD or CNY for each model. Converts all four rates when you change its currency.
- Shows separate USD and CNY totals when a session or turn uses both currencies.
- Keeps edits in a page draft. The **Save** button at the end of the page writes the configuration. Leaving the page discards unsaved edits. A failed save shows the error and keeps the draft.
- Shows two flat sections, **Model rates** and **General**, with all content visible. **General** contains the exchange rate, the session/turn visibility controls, the **Show cost statistics in the sidebar** switch (on by default) and the **Refresh cost statistics on a timer** switch (on by default). Turn the sidebar switch off to remove the sidebar entry; the overview page keeps its data. The timer switch has an interval list of 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60 minutes, with 5 minutes as the default. While it is on, the plugin loads the five preset ranges in parallel at that interval, so the overview page opens from the cache.
- Shows the cost overview page for today, 7, 30, 90 days, all history or a custom start and end date. It shows four summary figures, a stacked daily cost or token trend, the cost and token mix, cost by model, the top sessions and the current rate, totals and generation time. The trend uses daily bars; above 20 bars it merges neighbouring dates, and only the all-history range above 60 days with data switches to months. The model table lists every priced model. Amounts use the configured currency and `cnyPerUsd` rate.
- Caps the cost trend at 20 bars. Above 20 days it merges neighbouring dates and shows the merged span. The **Plugin settings** button opens the plugin page. Preset ranges cache their result for 15 minutes; **Refresh** or a price change recomputes it. The toolbar shows the cache state and the statistics time. Custom date ranges are not cached.
- Follows the DSH light or dark theme and the DSH Chinese or English language.
- Expands **More rates** on each model row to show its cache-write price and the automatic off-peak switch. The switch reveals that model's peak rule selector, and the info icon shows the windows of the selected rule.
- Adds a model by entering `provider/model` next to the **Model rates** title and selecting **Add model**. Declared models are saved with the configuration; models that history has not discovered can be removed.
- Marks invalid rates and exchange rates with a red border and a message, and disables **Save** and **Sync prices**.
- Reuses the DSH host controls (settings form, value field, switch, button and tag), so sizes, borders and colors match the host settings pages.
- Applies half the peak rate in each off-peak window. Each model selects one peak rule:
- **DeepSeek peak rule** (default): peak on Beijing weekday 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00; off-peak on weekends, Chinese public holidays and all other windows.
- **Alibaba Cloud peak rule**: off-peak 22:00–08:00 Beijing time; peak at all other times.
- **Zhipu GLM peak rule**: peak on Beijing Monday to Friday 14:00–18:00; off-peak at all other times, including the whole weekend.
- Uses holiday-cn annual calendars, cached under `data/holidays/`. Fetches a missing year in the background.
- Stores configuration at `~/.dsh/guojinpeng/dsh-cost-meter/config.json`. Uses `DSH_HOME` when set.
- Copies the old `~/.dsh/dsh-cost-meter/config.json` on first start if the new file does not exist. Keeps the old file.
- Uses isolated plugin, client, API, projection, style and configuration identifiers.

These screenshots use example model prices. They do not show a billing statement.

Existing model prices without a currency remain USD. Existing entries without an off-peak setting keep fixed rates until you switch it on. The switch is off by default for every new entry. Confirmed original-vendor DeepSeek off-peak rates from models.dev are multiplied by two to store peak rates. Every model applies its own selected rule; the default is the DeepSeek peak rule.

The configuration file stays at the same path. No configuration migration is required. Historical usage is replayed to restore dates and seven Beijing clock windows under projection state version 4. Requests that cross a price boundary are estimated from the recorded usage settlement time. Only the DeepSeek peak rule reads the holiday calendar; the Alibaba Cloud and GLM rules never need it. If a holiday calendar is unavailable, uncertain weekday windows use the peak rate until the calendar is loaded.

`priceSource` selects the cache for new models. Existing configuration without this field uses models.dev. Each model's `source` records its last price import; edits to rates on the configuration page set it to `manual`. Changing the selected source does not change existing rates or fetch prices. Cost calculation uses only the saved rates.

Caches are separate: `data/models.dev.json`, `data/openrouter.ai.json` and `data/api.deepinfra.com.json`. OpenRouter and DeepInfra prices are not multiplied by two. DeepSeek entries with automatic off-peak pricing keep their rates when the source cannot confirm an official peak rate. Sync reports show skipped models and cache-write rates that were kept because the cache duration is unclear. Conditional prices and non-token charges are outside this fixed-rate estimate.

Turn cost details:

![Turn cost card](docs/images/turn-cost-en.png)

Model price settings:

![Model price settings on desktop](docs/images/model-prices-desktop.png)
